question: Who among the following was the successor of Muhammad-Bin Tughlaq to the throne?
solution:
The Correct Answer is __**Firoz Shah Tuglaq**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• **Firoz Shah Tughlaq(1351-89)**

 
 
• After the death of Muhammad-bin**-Tughlaq** in 1351, he was chosen as sultan by the nobles.
 
• He strictly followed the advice of the ulemas in running the administration. 
 
• He pleased the nobles and assured hereditary succession to their properties. 
 
• Thus the iqta system was not only revived but also it was made hereditary.
 
• Four new taxes were introduced- 
 
 
• Kharaj - the land tax= 1/10 of the produce.
 
• Zakat - 2.5% tax on property.
 
• Jizya - protection tax paid by permanent non-muslims residents to rulers.
 
• Khams - 1/5th tax on Mines, treasure troves, and a share on war booty
 
 
 
• He was the first Sultan to impose an irrigation tax. 
 
• But at the same time, he dug irrigation canals and wells. 
 
• The longest canal was about 200 kilometres from Sutlej to Hansi. 
 
• Another canal was between Yamuna and Hissar.
 
• Diwani-i-Khairat -A department to make provisions for the marriage of poor girls was established.
 
• Dur-ul-Shifa - A hospital in Delhi was established.
 
• He started the imposition of Jizya on Brahmans.
 
• He imposed water cess Haq-i-shrib.
 
• Established four new towns, Firozabad, Fatehabad, Jaunpur, and Hissar.
 
• Firoz Shah's tomb is located in Hauz Khas (New Delhi), close to the tank built by Alauddin Khalji.​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• The sequence of Delhi sultanate Slave-Khilji**-Tughlaq-** Sayyid-Lodhi.
 
• The first Sayyid ruler of Delhi was Khizr Khan.
 
• The Lodi dynasty was founded by Bahlul Khan Lodi when he replaced the Sayyid dynasty

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• He was the founder of the Tughluq dynasty in India. 
 
• After assuming power, Ghazi Malik renamed himself Ghiyasuddin** Tughlaq**.
 
• After him, the dynasty was succeeded by his son Muhammad bin Tughluq.
 
• Rule of **Tughlaq dynasty (1320–1414)**.
 
• Rulers of the Tuglaq dynasty:
 
 
• 1321–1325 - Ghiyas-ud-din Tughlaq
 
• 1325–1351 - Muhammad Bin Tughlaq
 
• 1351–1388 - Firoz Shah Tughlaq
 
• 1388–1413 - Ghiyas-ud-din Tughluq Shah II/ Abu Bakr Shah / Muhammad Shah / Mahmud Tughlaq / Nusrat Shah.
 
 
 
• ​Ghiyas-ud-din Tughlaq
 
 
• He founded the city of Tughlaqabad.
 
• The cause of death is the structural collapse of plank on running elephants.
 
• He crushed the revolts in the unfriendly provinces with sturdy influence and resorted to harmony, law, and order
 
• He re-established the food laws of Ala-ud-Din
 
• He structured an improved postal system
 
• He encouraged agriculture in his Era.
 
 
 
• Muhammad bin** Tughlaq** 
 
 
• He was the Sultan of Delhi from 1325 to 1351 AD. 
 
• Muhammad Tughluq dreamt of making the whole of the Indian subcontinent his domain.
 
• Tughlaq attempted various administrative reforms, including the introduction of token currency and the shifting of the capital from Delhi to Daulatabad, which, though ambitious, faced significant challenges and were largely unsuccessful.
 
• Despite his reputation for eccentric policies, Tughlaq was a polymath with a keen interest in scholarship. He was well-versed in various disciplines, including philosophy, astronomy, and medicine.
